questions.q: Using the method 'Street Vending and Self-Employment', work with: other_workers = 2500, street_workers = 1200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_workers.
questions.a: 3700 persons

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Street Vending and Self-Employment' and work with: other_workers = 48000, street_workers = 1200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_workers.
questions.a: 49200 persons

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Street Vending and Self-Employment' refers to.
questions.a: Individuals who manage their own small-scale trade or services on city roadsides using temporary setups, carts, or pavement space.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Street Vending and Self-Employment'.
questions.a: Self-managed work with no employer and temporary physical structures.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Street Vending and Self-Employment', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_workers = street_workers + other_workers

questions.q: How much does a worker save if they earn {daily_earnings} and spend {daily_expenses}? Use the method 'Calculating Net Daily Savings'. Work with: daily_earnings = 40, daily_expenses = 5000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_savings.
questions.a: -4960 units

questions.q: Calculate the daily savings of a rickshaw puller earning {daily_earnings} with costs of {daily_expenses}. Use the method 'Calculating Net Daily Savings'. Work with: daily_earnings = 6, daily_expenses = 12000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_savings.
questions.a: -11994 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Calculating Net Daily Savings' refers to.
questions.a: The amount of money remaining with a worker after deducting daily living costs like food and rent from their total daily earnings.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Calculating Net Daily Savings'.
questions.a: The surplus income available to a worker for family support or future use.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Calculating Net Daily Savings', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: net_savings = daily_earnings - daily_expenses

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Legal Recognition of Hawkers' refers to.
questions.a: The policy shift recognizing street vending as a legitimate right to livelihood rather than just a traffic obstruction.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Legal Recognition of Hawkers'.
questions.a: Balancing the right to earn a living with the need for smooth traffic flow through hawking zones.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Legal Recognition of Hawkers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Working on the Street (source: fess309.txt lines 150-165)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Permanent Market Shops' refers to.
questions.a: Established retail businesses in designated market areas that hold municipal licenses and often hire supervisors and helpers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Permanent Market Shops'.
questions.a: Regulated commerce in fixed locations with formal licensing and staff management.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Permanent Market Shops' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: In the Market (source: fess309.txt lines 190-215)

concepts.title: Labour Chowk and Daily Wage Work

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Labour Chowk and Daily Wage Work' refers to.
questions.a: A specific location in a city where daily wage labourers gather to be hired by contractors for manual tasks.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Labour Chowk and Daily Wage Work'.
questions.a: Informal assembly point for casual workers seeking manual labor opportunities.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Labour Chowk and Daily Wage Work' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: In the Factory-Workshop Area (source: fess309.txt lines 235-250)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Casual Employment and Job Insecurity' refers to.
questions.a: A work arrangement where employees are hired on a temporary basis, usually during peak seasons, without long-term contracts or benefits.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Casual Employment and Job Insecurity'.
questions.a: Employment that lacks stability and depends entirely on the employer's immediate needs.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Casual Employment and Job Insecurity' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: In the Factory-Workshop Area (source: fess309.txt lines 275-300)

questions.q: Calculate the total daily pay if standard rate is {standard_rate} and overtime is {overtime_rate}. Use the method 'Total Daily Factory Wages'. Work with: overtime_rate = 20, standard_rate = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_daily_wage.
questions.a: 45 years

questions.q: Find the daily income of a tailor with {standard_rate} pay and {overtime_rate} for late work. Use the method 'Total Daily Factory Wages'. Work with: overtime_rate = 12, standard_rate = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_daily_wage.
questions.a: 20 years

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Total Daily Factory Wages' refers to.
questions.a: The total compensation a factory worker receives for a day, including their base pay for standard hours and extra pay for overtime.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Total Daily Factory Wages'.
questions.a: Summing regular pay and additional incentives for extra work hours.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Total Daily Factory Wages', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_daily_wage = standard_rate + overtime_rate

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Regular and Permanent Employment' refers to.
questions.a: Stable jobs in offices or government departments where workers receive a regular monthly salary and have long-term job security.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Regular and Permanent Employment'.
questions.a: Consistent employment with a fixed workplace and predictable income.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Regular and Permanent Employment' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: In the office area (source: fess309.txt lines 325-350)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Social Security and Employee Benefits' refers to.
questions.a: Additional financial and health protections provided to permanent workers, such as provident funds, medical insurance, and paid leave.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Social Security and Employee Benefits'.
questions.a: Non-wage compensation that supports a worker's health and retirement.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Social Security and Employee Benefits' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: In the office area (source: fess309.txt lines 335-345)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Call Centres in Big Cities' refers to.
questions.a: Centralized offices equipped with computers and telephones to handle consumer queries and services for domestic or foreign companies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Call Centres in Big Cities'.
questions.a: A modern form of urban employment providing services via telecommunication.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Call Centres in Big Cities' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: In the office area (source: fess309.txt lines 315-325)
